subject: gk
question: Statutory grants to states by the Union government, under Article 275 of the Constitution, are primarily recommended by which body?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Finance Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body established under **Article 280** of the Indian Constitution to recommend financial relations between the Union and the States.
 
• Under **Article 275**, the Finance Commission recommends statutory grants to states to ensure balanced regional development and mitigate disparities.
 
• These grants are given to states that require financial assistance to meet specific needs, such as social welfare, infrastructure development, or education.
 
• The Finance Commission submits its recommendations to the President, which are then tabled in Parliament for implementation.
 
• The grants are unconditional and are intended to supplement the resources of the states to enable them to perform their constitutional responsibilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Finance Commission:**

 
 
• Constituted every five years or earlier as deemed necessary by the President.
 
• Composed of a Chairperson and four other members with expertise in public finance and governance.
 
• The 15th Finance Commission, chaired by **N.K. Singh**, submitted its report for 2021-26.
 
 
 
• **Article 275:**
 
 
• Empowers Parliament to make grants-in-aid to states, as recommended by the Finance Commission.
 
• These grants aim to promote the welfare of Scheduled Tribes and develop their areas.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Ministry of Finance:**
 
 
• Although the Finance Commission makes recommendations, the Ministry of Finance oversees the disbursement of grants to states.
 
• It ensures that funds are allocated as per constitutional provisions and Commission recommendations.
 
 
 
• **Difference from NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• NITI Aayog focuses on policy formulation and cooperative federalism, while the Finance Commission deals with financial resource allocation.
 
• NITI Aayog does not have a constitutional mandate to recommend statutory grants.
